mainTopic: Sources in the תורה for תחיית המתים, debates with outsiders about it, and the side topic of giving תרומה only to a כהן who is careful with the תורה
overview: This amud opens by finishing a proof of מדה כנגד מדה: the officer who mocked אלישע at the city gate was trampled in that same gate. The extra word 'בשער' shows this was his punishment, not just אלישע's curse. Next, רבי יוחנן finds תחיית המתים in the תורה from the command to give תרומה 'to אהרן', who never entered ארץ ישראל. That leads to a side discussion: תרומה should go only to a כהן who is a חבר. Giving it to a כהן עם הארץ is like putting it before a lion, can cause his death, and brings sin upon him. The גמרא then gathers more proofs for תחיית המתים: from רבי סימאי, from רבן גמליאל's debate with the צדוקים, from רבי יהושע בן חנניה's answer to the Romans, and from רבי אליעזר ברבי יוסי against the כותים. Along the way, רבי עקיבא and רבי ישמעאל argue about how to read 'הכרת תכרת', and a ברייתא teaches that תשובה saves a person from כרת. The amud ends with stories: רבי מאיר tells קליאופטרא that the righteous will rise clothed. Then the emperor challenges רבן גמליאל that dust cannot live, and the answer comes on the next amud.

steps.title: The officer was trampled in the gate
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes its proof of מדה כנגד מדה with the פסוק describing how the officer died.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it is written: 'And so it happened to him: the people trampled him in the gate, and he died.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a proof it began just before this section. It quotes the פסוק describing how the officer who mocked אלישע died.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The officer had doubted אלישע's prophecy of cheap food. אלישע told him he would see it but not eat it. This פסוק shows how that came true: he was trampled to death in the gate, and the גמרא uses this as an example of מדה כנגד מדה.

keyTerms.meaning: And it is written (introducing a second פסוק)
Measure for measure: the punishment matches the sin

phrases.english: And it is written: 'And so it was for him,'
phrases.notes: This continues a proof that began just before this section. 'So' means exactly what אלישע had said would happen to him.

phrases.english: 'and the people trampled him in the gate,'
'and he died.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the proof of מדה כנגד מדה that began before this section.
steps.raayaObject: The הקב"ה punishes מדה כנגד מדה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: מלכים ב 7:20: the officer who mocked the prophecy was trampled in the gate and died.

steps.title: Maybe it was just אלישע's curse
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the proof: perhaps the officer died because of אלישע's curse, not because of מדה כנגד מדה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But perhaps it was אלישע's curse that caused his death? After all, רב יהודה said in the name of רב: the curse of a חכם comes true even if it was undeserved.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof. Maybe the officer died only because a great prophet cursed him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If even an undeserved curse of a חכם comes true, a deserved curse from אלישע certainly would. In that case his death proves nothing about the הקב"ה's system of מדה כנגד מדה.

keyTerms.meaning: The curse of a Torah scholar
For nothing, without a real reason

phrases.english: But perhaps the curse of Elisha caused it to him?
phrases.notes: The curse is אלישע's words to him: 'you will see it with your eyes, but you will not eat from it.'

phrases.english: As Rav Yehuda said in the name of Rav:

phrases.aramaic: קִלְלַת חָכָם, אֲפִילּוּ עַל חִנָּם הִיא בָּאָה.
phrases.english: The curse of a sage, even if for nothing, it comes true.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the proof brought in step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: The use of the officer's death as proof of מדה כנגד מדה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: There is another explanation for his death: a חכם's curse always comes true, so the death may just be the curse coming true.

steps.title: The word 'in the gate' shows it was measure for measure
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the extra word 'בשער' shows the death was tied to what he did at the gate.
steps.simpleTranslation: If it were only the curse, the פסוק should have said 'they trampled him and he died.' Why add 'in the gate'? To show it was because of matters of the gate.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. It points to an extra word in the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A curse would only explain that he died. The פסוק stresses the place, 'in the gate', which is where he had mocked the prophecy of cheap food being sold at the gate. So the place of his death matches his sin, which is מדה כנגד מדה.
steps.whatToRemember: The extra word 'בשער' shows that the officer's death matched his sin, so the proof of מדה כנגד מדה stands.

phrases.english: If so, let the verse write:
'And they trampled him and he died.'
What is 'in the gate' for?
Because of matters of the gate.
phrases.notes: He mocked the prophecy about food being sold at the gate, so he died at that very gate.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reading a seemingly extra word in the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: His death could be explained by אלישע's curse alone.
steps.terutzMaskana: The added 'בשער' ties his death to his sin at the gate, which shows מדה כנגד מדה.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן looks for תחיית המתים in the תורה
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן asks where the תורה hints at תחיית המתים, and cites the command to give תרומה to אהרן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: Where do we see תחיית המתים in the תורה? As it says: 'And you shall give from it the תרומה of ה׳ to אהרן the כהן.'
steps.whatsHappening: A new statement begins. רבי יוחנן asks for a source and quotes a פסוק; the next step explains how the פסוק proves it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is not whether תחיית המתים is true. It is where the תורה itself hints at it. The answer comes from a מצוה about giving תרומת מעשר to 'אהרן'.

keyTerms.meaning: A portion of produce given to a כהן

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
From where do we know the resurrection of the dead from the Torah?
As it is said: 'And you shall give from it the teruma of the Lord'
phrases.notes: The word in square brackets is added in the corrected wording, to match the פסוק.

phrases.english: 'to Aaron the priest.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new series of sources for תחיית המתים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There is a source in the תורה for תחיית המתים: the פסוק commanding תרומה be given to אהרן.

steps.title: אהרן never entered the Land, so he will live again
steps.stepSummary: Since אהרן died before entering ארץ ישראל, where תרומה is given, the פסוק must mean he will come back to life.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does אהרן live forever? He never even entered ארץ ישראל, where they give him תרומה! Rather, this teaches that he will live in the future, and ישראל will give him תרומה. From here we see תחיית המתים in the תורה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how the פסוק proves תחיית המתים. Its point is that the plain meaning of the words cannot have been fulfilled in אהרן's lifetime.
steps.deeperAnalysis: תרומה was given only after entering ארץ ישראל, and אהרן died in the desert. So the command to give תרומה 'to אהרן' himself can only be fulfilled if he comes back to life. That shows the תורה assumes תחיית המתים.

keyTerms.meaning: And is it so that...? (a question that expects 'no')
Will live again in the future

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן: 'give תרומה to אהרן' must be fulfilled after תחיית המתים, because אהרן died before תרומה was ever given.
steps.confusionAlert: The question 'does אהרן live forever?' is not a challenge to רבי יוחנן. It is part of his own proof, showing the פסוק can't mean the plain present-day sense.

phrases.english: And does Aaron live forever?
But did he not fail to enter the Land of Israel,
where they would give him teruma!
Rather, it teaches that he is destined to live again,
and the Jewish people will give him teruma.
From here we learn the resurrection of the dead from the Torah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how the פסוק cited in step 4 proves תחיית המתים.
steps.raayaObject: תחיית המתים has a source in the תורה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: במדבר 18:28: the command to give תרומה to אהרן himself, who never entered ארץ ישראל.

steps.title: 'To אהרן' means 'like אהרן'
steps.stepSummary: דבי רבי ישמעאל read 'לאהרן' as 'כאהרן': תרומה goes only to a כהן who is a חבר, like אהרן.
steps.simpleTranslation: The school of רבי ישמעאל taught: 'To אהרן' means 'like אהרן.' Just as אהרן was a חבר, so too his descendants who receive תרומה must be חברים.
steps.whatsHappening: A different teaching reads the same word 'לאהרן' in another way. It uses it for a practical rule about which כהנים receive תרומה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of reading the פסוק as speaking to אהרן himself (which led רבי יוחנן to תחיית המתים), this ברייתא reads it as describing the kind of כהן who gets תרומה. A חבר is someone careful with the laws of טהרה, תרומה and מעשרות, so תרומה goes to a כהן like that.

keyTerms.meaning: The school of רבי ישמעאל taught
A person careful with the laws of purity and tithes

phrases.english: The school of Rabbi Yishmael taught:
'To Aaron' means like Aaron:
just as Aaron was a chaver,
so too his sons must be chaverim.
phrases.notes: 'His sons' means the כהנים descended from him who receive the תרומה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reads the same word 'לאהרן' from step 4 in a different way, for a practical law.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: תרומה is given only to a כהן who is a חבר, like אהרן.

steps.title: No תרומה for a כהן who is an עם הארץ
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמואל בר נחמני in the name of רבי יונתן proves from דברי הימים that only a כהן who holds onto the תורה gets a portion.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמואל בר נחמני said in the name of רבי יונתן: How do we know we don't give תרומה to a כהן who is an עם הארץ? The פסוק says the people of ירושלים were told to give the portion of the כהנים and לויים 'so that they hold firm to the תורה of ה׳.' Whoever holds firm to the תורה has a portion; whoever doesn't, has no portion.
steps.whatsHappening: Another אמורא gives a source for a similar rule: a כהן who is an עם הארץ does not receive תרומה. He reads the purpose clause of the פסוק as a requirement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says the gifts are given 'so that' the כהנים can devote themselves to the תורה. רבי יונתן learns from this that the gift belongs only to those who actually hold onto the תורה. So a כהן who ignores the תורה loses his right to the portion.

keyTerms.meaning: A person ignorant of or careless with Torah law

steps.whatToRemember: Both דבי רבי ישמעאל and רבי יונתן teach that תרומה goes to a כהן who is careful with the תורה, not to an עם הארץ.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר נַחְמָנִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹנָתָן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachmani said in the name of Rabbi Yonatan:
From where do we know that one does not give teruma
to a priest who is an am ha'aretz?
As it is said: 'And he told the people, the dwellers of Jerusalem,'
'to give the portion of the priests and the Levites,'
'so that they may hold firmly to the Torah of the Lord.'

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל הַמַּחְזִיק בְּתוֹרַת ה׳ – יֵשׁ לוֹ מְנָת,
phrases.english: Whoever holds firmly to the Torah of the Lord has a portion,

phrases.aramaic: וְשֶׁאֵינוֹ מַחְזִיק בְּתוֹרַת ה׳ – אֵין לוֹ מְנָת.
phrases.english: and whoever does not hold firmly to the Torah of the Lord has no portion.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִנַּיִין שֶׁאֵין נוֹתְנִין תְּרוּמָה לְכֹהֵן עַם הָאָרֶץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives another source for the idea in step 6, that תרומה goes only to a כהן who is careful with the תורה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One does not give תרומה to a כהן who is an עם הארץ, because only one who holds firmly to the תורה has a portion.

steps.title: Giving תרומה to an unlearned כהן is like putting it before a lion
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה teaches that giving תרומה to a כהן עם הארץ is like putting it in front of a lion. You cannot know whether he will eat it in purity or in impurity.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא בר אדא said in the name of רב יהודה: Whoever gives תרומה to a כהן who is an עם הארץ is like someone who places it in front of a lion. With a lion, maybe it mauls its prey and then eats it, and maybe it eats it without mauling it first. So too with a כהן עם הארץ: maybe he eats the תרומה in purity, and maybe he eats it in impurity.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new teaching that builds on Step 7: do not give תרומה to a כהן who does not know or keep the תורה. It uses a picture of a lion to show the danger.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the food is in front of a lion, the owner has no control over what happens to it. In the same way, a כהן עם הארץ does not know or keep the laws of purity carefully. So the giver cannot be sure the holy תרומה will be eaten the right way.

keyTerms.meaning: An unlearned person who is not careful with the laws of purity and the like

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב אַחָא בַּר אַדָּא אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה:
phrases.english: Rav Acha bar Adda said that Rav Yehuda said:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל הַנּוֹתֵן תְּרוּמָה לְכֹהֵן עַם הָאָרֶץ,
phrases.english: Anyone who gives teruma to a priest who is an am ha'aretz,
it is as if he places it before a lion.
Just as a lion: maybe it mauls and eats,
maybe it does not maul, and eats,
so too a priest who is an am ha'aretz:
maybe he eats it in purity,
maybe he eats it in impurity.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אַחָא בַּר אַדָּא אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה: כׇּל הַנּוֹתֵן תְּרוּמָה לְכֹהֵן עַם הָאָרֶץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a warning to Step 7's rule that only a כהן who holds onto the תורה should get תרומה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Giving תרומה to a כהן עם הארץ is like putting it before a lion, because he may eat it in impurity.

steps.title: The giver even causes the כהן's death
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן adds that giving תרומה to a כהן עם הארץ can even cause the כהן to deserve death, as the פסוק says about one who makes תרומה impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: He even causes the כהן's death, as it says, 'And they will die through it, because they made it חולין.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן makes the warning from Step 8 stronger. The giver does not only risk the תרומה being eaten in impurity. He can even cause the כהן to die.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says a כהן who eats תרומה in impurity is punished with death. Since a כהן עם הארץ may well eat it in impurity, the person who handed it to him shares in causing that punishment.

keyTerms.meaning: Death (here, a death penalty from Heaven)
They make it חולין (they disrespect something holy)

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
He even causes him death,
phrases.notes: 'He' is the giver, and 'him' is the כהן עם הארץ.

phrases.english: as it is said: 'And they will die through it, because they profane it.'

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: אַף גּוֹרֵם לוֹ מִיתָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on Step 8 with a more serious result: death.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Giving תרומה to a כהן עם הארץ can cause his death, based on ויקרא 22:9.

steps.title: The giver also brings sin upon the כהן
steps.stepSummary: The school of רבי אליעזר בן יעקב taught that the giver also loads the כהן with a 'sin of guilt', as the פסוק says.
steps.simpleTranslation: The school of רבי אליעזר בן יעקב taught: He also loads him with a sin of guilt, as it says, 'And they will bring upon them a sin of guilt when they eat their holy things.'
steps.whatsHappening: A third teaching adds one more harm caused by the giver: he brings sin onto the כהן. This closes the short section about the כהן עם הארץ.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק speaks about people who cause others to eat holy food in a way that is not allowed. The school of רבי אליעזר בן יעקב reads it as describing the giver. By handing the תרומה over, he makes himself part of the כהן's sin.

keyTerms.meaning: Loads him with, brings upon him

steps.whatToRemember: Three teachings in a row (Steps 8 to 10) warn that giving תרומה to a כהן עם הארץ is dangerous. It is like feeding a lion, it can cause his death, and it brings sin upon him.

phrases.aramaic: דְּבֵי רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב תָּנָא:
phrases.english: The school of Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov taught:
He also loads him with a sin of guilt,
as it is said: 'And they will bring upon them a sin of guilt'
'when they eat their holy things.'

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּבֵי רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב תָּנָא: אַף מַשִּׂיאוֹ עֲוֹן אַשְׁמָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a third harm after Steps 8 and 9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Giving תרומה to a כהן עם הארץ brings a sin of guilt upon him, based on ויקרא 22:16.

steps.title: רבי סימאי proves תחיית המתים from the word 'to them'
steps.stepSummary: רבי סימאי proves תחיית המתים from the תורה‎. ה׳ promised to give ארץ כנען 'to them', meaning to the אבות themselves. They never received it while alive, so they must come back to life to receive it.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא teaches that רבי סימאי says: Where do we learn תחיית המתים from the תורה? As it says: 'And I also set up My covenant with them, to give them the land of כנען.' It does not say 'to you' but 'to them.' From here we learn תחיית המתים from the תורה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the main question from Step 4: where does the תורה hint at תחיית המתים? It brings a second proof, from רבי סימאי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The promise was made to the אבות, but they died before the land was given. If the פסוק meant their children, it could have said 'to you' (the people ה׳ was speaking to in משה's time). Saying 'to them' means the אבות themselves will receive the land, so they must come back to life. This proof works the same way as the אהרן proof in Step 5.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in a ברייתא
The dead coming back to life

phrases.english: It was taught: Rabbi Simai says:
From where is resurrection of the dead learned from the Torah?
As it is said: 'And I also established My covenant with them,'
phrases.notes: שמות 6:4. 'Them' means the אבות: אברהם, יצחק and יעקב.

phrases.english: 'to give them the land of Canaan.'
'To you' is not said, but rather 'to them.'
From here we learn resurrection of the dead from the Torah.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא, רַבִּי סִימַאי אוֹמֵר: מִנַּיִין לִתְחִיַּית הַמֵּתִים מִן הַתּוֹרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the side topic of the כהן עם הארץ and returns to proofs for תחיית המתים.
steps.raayaObject: That תחיית המתים is hinted at in the תורה
steps.raayaSupportSource: שמות 6:4, 'to give them the land of כנען'
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The word 'להם' shows the אבות themselves will get the land, so they will come back to life.

steps.title: The צדוקים ask רבן גמליאל for a source for תחיית המתים
steps.stepSummary: After a memory aid, the גמרא tells how צדוקים asked רבן גמליאל how we know that ה׳ brings the dead back to life.
steps.simpleTranslation: (Memory aid: צדק, גם, גשם, קם.) The צדוקים asked רבן גמליאל: How do we know that the Holy One, Blessed be He, brings the dead back to life?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a longer story. First it gives a memory aid for the proofs that will follow, then it brings the צדוקים' question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The צדוקים did not believe in תחיית המתים. They challenge רבן גמליאל to show a source. This sets up a series of proofs and arguments in the coming lines.

keyTerms.meaning: A memory aid made of key words
A group that rejected the תורה שבעל פה and תחיית המתים
Brings the dead back to life

phrases.english: (Tzedek, Gam, Geshem, Kam: a mnemonic)
phrases.notes: A memory aid with key words from the discussion that follows. Some versions print it and some don't.

phrases.english: The Sadducees asked Rabban Gamliel:

phrases.aramaic: מִנַּיִין שֶׁהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא מְחַיֶּיה מֵתִים?
phrases.english: From where do we know that the Holy One, Blessed be He, revives the dead?

steps.triggerLanguage: שָׁאֲלוּ צַדּוּקִים אֶת רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל: מִנַּיִין שֶׁהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא מְחַיֶּיה מֵתִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from a ברייתא proof to a story of a debate about the same topic.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source showing that ה׳ will bring the dead back to life

steps.title: רבן גמליאל says there are proofs from all of תנ"ך, but they reject them
steps.stepSummary: רבן גמליאל answers that there are proofs from תורה, נביאים, and כתובים, but the צדוקים did not accept them.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: From the תורה, from the נביאים, and from the כתובים. But they did not accept it from him.
steps.whatsHappening: רבן גמליאל gives a general answer: all three parts of תנ"ך show תחיית המתים. This sets up the next lines, where the גמרא will spell out each proof and the צדוקים' push-back.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'they did not accept it from him' tell us the צדוקים had a way to explain away each פסוק. This prepares us for the back-and-forth that comes next.
steps.confusionAlert: Being told 'they did not accept' does not mean רבן גמליאל's proofs were weak. The צדוקים simply found other ways to read the פסוקים, and the גמרא will show the full debate next.

phrases.english: He said to them: From the Torah,
and from the Prophets, and from the Writings.
But they did not accept it from him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָהֶם: מִן הַתּוֹרָה, וּמִן הַנְּבִיאִים, וּמִן הַכְּתוּבִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the צדוקים' question from Step 12 in general terms.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: תחיית המתים can be shown from תורה, נביאים, and כתובים, though the צדוקים rejected it.

steps.title: First proof from the Torah: 'you will lie with your fathers and rise'
steps.stepSummary: רבן גמליאל quotes ה׳ telling משה that he will lie with his fathers and then 'rise'.
steps.simpleTranslation: From the תורה, as it is written: 'And ה׳ said to משה: Behold, you will lie with your fathers and rise.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבן גמליאל gives his first proof, from the תורה. משה is told he will die ('lie with your fathers') and then 'rise'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Lying with your fathers means dying. If the next word, 'and rise', goes with משה, then משה will come back to life after death. That would be תחיית המתים.

keyTerms.meaning: From the תורה (the five books of משה)
Lie with your fathers, a way of saying 'die'

phrases.english: From the Torah, as it is written:
"And ה׳ said to Moshe:
Behold, you will lie with your fathers, and rise."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the first of the three proofs that step 13 said רבן גמליאל brought.

steps.title: The צדוקים read 'rise' as going with the people, not משה
steps.stepSummary: The צדוקים say 'and rise' belongs to the next words: 'this people will rise and stray'.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: But perhaps it means 'and this people will rise and stray'?
steps.whatsHappening: The צדוקים push aside the proof. They say the word 'rise' starts the next part of the פסוק and is about the Jewish people, not משה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The whole proof rested on the word 'וְקָם' belonging to משה. The rest of the פסוק says 'וְקָם הָעָם הַזֶּה וְזָנָה', meaning the people will rise up and stray after other gods. If 'וְקָם' goes there, the פסוק says nothing about משה coming back to life.

keyTerms.meaning: But perhaps, used to suggest another way to read something

phrases.english: They said to him:
But perhaps it is "and this people will rise and stray"?
phrases.notes: These are the next words in the very same פסוק, so 'rise' could belong to them instead.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of step 14.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The word 'וְקָם' can be read with the words after it, about the people straying, and not with משה.

steps.title: Second proof from the Prophets: 'Your dead will live'
steps.stepSummary: רבן גמליאל quotes ישעיה: the dead will live, those in the dust will wake up and sing.
steps.simpleTranslation: From the נביאים, as it is written: 'Your dead will live, my corpses will rise. Wake up and sing, you who dwell in the dust, for your dew is a dew of light, and the earth will cast out the dead.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבן גמליאל gives his second proof, now from the נביאים. The פסוק openly says the dead will live and rise from the dust.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here no one can argue about which word goes where, because the פסוק plainly talks about dead people coming back to life. The only question left is which dead people it means.

keyTerms.meaning: Those who dwell in the dust, meaning the dead in their graves

phrases.english: From the Prophets, as it is written:
"Your dead will live, my corpses will rise,
wake up and sing, you who dwell in the dust,
for your dew is a dew of light,
and the earth will cast out the dead."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the תורה proof was pushed aside, רבן גמליאל moves to a proof from the נביאים.

steps.title: The צדוקים say it means the dead that יחזקאל revived
steps.stepSummary: The צדוקים say the פסוק already came true when יחזקאל brought the dry bones back to life.
steps.simpleTranslation: But perhaps it means the dead that יחזקאל brought back to life?
steps.whatsHappening: The צדוקים push aside the second proof. They agree the פסוק is about dead people living, but say it was a one-time event that already happened.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבן גמליאל needs a promise that all the dead will come back in the future. The צדוקים say the פסוק could be about the dead that יחזקאל revived long ago. That would not prove a future תחיית המתים for everyone.

keyTerms.meaning: The נביא who saw the vision of the dry bones coming to life
That he brought back to life

phrases.english: But perhaps it means the dead whom Yechezkel brought back to life?
phrases.notes: The צדוקים are still the ones talking. This is the story of the dry bones in יחזקאל 37.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of step 16.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The פסוק may be about a past, one-time revival by יחזקאל, not a future תחיית המתים.

steps.title: Third proof from the Writings: 'moving the lips of those who sleep'
steps.stepSummary: רבן גמליאל quotes שיר השירים, which speaks of the lips of 'those who sleep' moving.
steps.simpleTranslation: From the כתובים, as it is written: 'And your palate is like the best wine, going to my beloved smoothly, moving the lips of those who sleep.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבן גמליאל gives his third proof, now from the כתובים. He reads 'those who sleep' as the dead, whose lips will move again.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the dead speak again, they must be alive again. So the פסוק would hint that the dead will one day rise.

keyTerms.meaning: The Writings, the third part of תנ״ך
Those who sleep, here meaning the dead

phrases.english: From the Writings, as it is written:
"And your palate is like the best wine,
going to my beloved smoothly,
moving the lips of those who sleep."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the נביאים proof was pushed aside, רבן גמליאל moves to a proof from the כתובים.

steps.title: The צדוקים say the lips only move in the grave
steps.stepSummary: The צדוקים say the lips may only move in the grave, as רבי יוחנן teaches about one whose הלכה is repeated.
steps.simpleTranslation: But perhaps their lips just move a little? This would match רבי יוחנן, who said in the name of רבי שמעון בן יהוצדק: anyone whose הלכה is said in his name in this world, his lips move in the grave, as it says, 'moving the lips of those who sleep.'
steps.whatsHappening: The צדוקים push aside the third proof. They say the פסוק only means a dead person's lips move in the grave, not that he comes back to life.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא backs up their reading with a teaching of רבי יוחנן. When people repeat a הלכה in someone's name, his lips move in the grave. That uses the same פסוק but has nothing to do with rising from the dead, so the proof falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: A הלכה said in his name

phrases.english: But perhaps their lips merely move?
In line with Rabbi Yochanan,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יְהוֹצָדָק:
phrases.english: as Rabbi Yochanan said in the name of Rabbi Shimon ben Yehotzadak:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל מִי שֶׁנֶּאֶמְרָה הֲלָכָה בִּשְׁמוֹ בְּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה,
phrases.english: Anyone in whose name a halacha is said in this world,
his lips move in the grave,
as it is said: "moving the lips of those who sleep."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of step 18.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The פסוק may only mean lips moving in the grave, as in רבי יוחנן's teaching, and not real coming back to life.
steps.whyThisMatters: Along the way the גמרא teaches the well-known idea that repeating a הלכה in its author's name makes his lips move in the grave.

steps.title: The final proof: the land was promised 'to them'
steps.stepSummary: רבן גמליאל quotes the promise to give the land 'to them', the אבות. This proves תחיית המתים from the תורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Until he said to them this פסוק: 'that ה׳ swore to your fathers to give to them.' It does not say 'to you' but 'to them'. From here we learn תחיית המתים from the תורה.
steps.whatsHappening: After three proofs were pushed aside, רבן גמליאל brings one more that settles the matter. The land was promised to the אבות themselves, who never got it while alive.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ה׳ swore to give the land 'to them', the אבות, not 'to you', their children. The אבות died without owning the land, so for the promise to come true they must come back to life. This works the same way as רבי סימאי's proof in step 11, but uses a different פסוק (דברים 11:21, not שמות 6:4).

keyTerms.meaning: Bringing the dead back to life

steps.whatToRemember: The first three proofs could each be read another way. The winning proof rests on one small word, 'לָהֶם‎': ה׳'s promise to the אבות themselves can only come true if they come back to life.
steps.confusionAlert: The פסוק is talking to the children ('your fathers'), but it says the land goes 'to them', the fathers. Do not mix up who is being spoken to with who receives the land.

phrases.english: Until he said to them this verse:
"That ה׳ swore to your fathers to give to them."
It does not say "to you," but rather "to them."
From here we learn resurrection of the dead from the Torah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the three rejected proofs (steps 14-19), this proof finally settles the debate.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: תחיית המתים is learned from the תורה, because ה׳ promised the land to the אבות themselves, and they must come back to life to receive it.

steps.title: Another version of רבן גמליאל's final proof
steps.stepSummary: Some say רבן גמליאל's winning proof was the פסוק 'you who cling to ה' are all alive today.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say this is the פסוק רבן גמליאל told them: 'And you who cling to ה' your God are all alive today.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a different version of which פסוק רבן גמליאל used to finally convince the people he was debating. This step only quotes the פסוק; the next steps explain how it proves תחיית המתים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 20, the final proof was the promise to give the land 'to them,' the אבות. Here a second opinion says the winning proof was a different פסוק from דברים. How this פסוק proves anything is not clear yet, and the גמרא will now explain it.

phrases.aramaic: וְיֵשׁ אוֹמְרִים: מִן הַמִּקְרָא הַזֶּה אָמַר לָהֶם,
phrases.english: And some say: it was from this verse that he told them,
phrases.notes: 'He' is רבן גמליאל, giving his final proof from step 20.

phrases.english: "And you who cling to the Lord your God
are all of you alive today."

steps.triggerLanguage: וְיֵשׁ אוֹמְרִים: מִן הַמִּקְרָא הַזֶּה אָמַר לָהֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different version of the final proof from step 20.
steps.raayaObject: תחיית המתים is in the תורה

steps.title: Isn't it obvious they were alive that day?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: of course the people משה was speaking to were alive! Why does the פסוק need to say it?
steps.simpleTranslation: It is obvious that they were all alive that day!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that the words 'you are all alive today' seem to be extra, since everyone משה was talking to was obviously alive. This sets up the explanation that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying 'you are alive' to living people adds nothing on the plain level. Because the words seem extra, they must be teaching something more. That 'something more' is what makes this פסוק a proof.

keyTerms.meaning: It is obvious! (a challenge that something did not need to be said)

phrases.english: It is obvious that you are all alive today!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the wording of the פסוק quoted in step 21.
steps.kashyaTarget: The words 'alive today' in the פסוק
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Telling living people they are alive seems pointless.

steps.title: Alive even when everyone has died
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק means: just as you are all alive today, you will all be alive in עולם הבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it means: even on the day when the whole world is dead, you will be alive. Just as today you are all alive, so too in עולם הבא you will all be alive.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that the extra words are a promise for the future. You will be alive in עולם הבא just as you are alive today.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'today' becomes a comparison: your life today is a model for your life later. Since this life will come after death, the פסוק is a source for תחיית המתים.
steps.whatToRemember: The extra words 'alive today' teach that just as Israel is alive now, they will be alive again in עולם הבא.

phrases.english: Rather, even on the day when the whole world
are all dead, you are alive.
Just as today all of you are alive,
so too in the World to Come all of you will be alive.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 22 by explaining the extra words.
steps.terutzMaskana: They promise life in עולם הבא, just like life today.

steps.title: The Romans ask רבי יהושע בן חנניה for a source
steps.stepSummary: The Romans ask for a source that הקדוש ברוך הוא brings the dead back to life and knows the future.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Romans asked רבי יהושע בן חנניה: Where do we see that הקדוש ברוך הוא brings the dead back to life, and that He knows what will happen in the future?
steps.whatsHappening: A new story begins. The Romans ask רבי יהושע בן חנניה for a source for two ideas: תחיית המתים and that ה' knows the future.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is another debate with outsiders, like רבן גמליאל's debate with the צדוקים. The question has two parts, and that matters, because the answer will cover both parts with one פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: Brings the dead back to life
What is going to happen in the future

phrases.aramaic: שָׁאֲלוּ רוֹמִיִּים אֶת רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן חֲנַנְיָה:
phrases.english: The Romans asked Rabbi Yehoshua ben Ḥananya:

phrases.aramaic: מִנַּיִין שֶׁהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא מְחַיֵּה מֵתִים,
phrases.english: From where do we know that the Holy One, Blessed be He, brings the dead back to life,
and that He knows what will happen in the future?

steps.triggerLanguage: שָׁאֲלוּ רוֹמִיִּים אֶת רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן חֲנַנְיָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new story with a new search for a source for תחיית המתים.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source for תחיית המתים and for ה' knowing the future

steps.title: Both ideas come from one פסוק about משה
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע answers from 'you will lie with your fathers and rise; this people will stray.'
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: Both come from this פסוק: 'ה' said to משה: You will lie with your fathers and rise up. This people will stray.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע בן חנניה answers both questions with one פסוק. He reads the word 'and rise' as going on משה: משה will die and then rise again.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Read this way, the פסוק has two parts. 'You will lie with your fathers and rise' means משה dies and later comes back to life, which is תחיית המתים. 'This people will stray' is ה' telling the future, which shows He knows what will happen.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לְהוּ: תַּרְוַויְיהוּ מִן הַמִּקְרָא הַזֶּה,
phrases.english: He said to them: Both of them come from this verse,
as it says: "And the Lord said to Moses,
Behold, you will lie with your fathers and rise;
phrases.notes: He reads 'and rise' as going with משה: משה dies, then rises.

phrases.english: this people will go astray."

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לְהוּ: תַּרְוַויְיהוּ מִן הַמִּקְרָא הַזֶּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the Romans' question from step 24.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: דברים 31:16, read as 'משה will lie and rise' (תחיית המתים) plus 'this people will stray' (knowing the future).

steps.title: Maybe 'rise' goes with 'the people'
steps.stepSummary: The Romans suggest reading 'and this people will rise up and stray', which says nothing about משה rising.
steps.simpleTranslation: But maybe it means: 'And this people will rise up and stray'?
steps.whatsHappening: The Romans push back on the proof. They say the word 'and rise' can go with the next words instead, so the פסוק means the people will rise up and go astray.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Hebrew פסוקים can be divided in more than one place. If 'and rise' belongs to 'this people,' then nobody is rising from the dead. משה just dies, and afterward the people get up and sin. This removes the proof for תחיית המתים.

keyTerms.meaning: But maybe (suggesting another way to read)

steps.confusionAlert: The Romans are not changing any words of the פסוק. They are only moving where the sentence breaks: 'and rise' could finish משה's part or start the people's part.

phrases.english: But maybe it is: "And this people will rise up and go astray"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reading of the פסוק given in step 25.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the תחיית המתים half of the proof
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The word 'and rise' may belong to 'this people,' not to משה.

steps.title: At least take half the proof
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע admits the point and says: at least the proof that ה' knows the future still stands.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: At least hold on to half in your hands: that He knows what will happen in the future.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע בן חנניה does not fight the Romans' reading. He says that either way, half of his proof still works: ה' knows the future.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Whichever way you divide the פסוק, ה' is telling משה ahead of time that the people will stray. So the 'knowing the future' part is safe. רבי יהושע does not defend the תחיית המתים half here. The next step brings support for reading the פסוק that way.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לְהוּ: נְקוּטוּ מִיהָא פַּלְגָא בִּידַיְיכוּ,
phrases.english: He said to them: At least take half into your hands,
that He knows what will happen in the future.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to the challenge of step 26 by keeping part of the proof.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The whole proof falls apart because of the other reading.
steps.terutzMaskana: At least the proof that ה' knows the future stands either way.

steps.title: רבי שמעון בן יוחאי uses the same פסוק
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן, quoting רבי שמעון בן יוחאי, learns both ideas from the same פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also said: רבי יוחנן said in the name of רבי שמעון בן יוחאי: From where do we know that הקדוש ברוך הוא brings the dead back to life and knows the future? Because it says: 'You will lie with your fathers and rise, etc.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings support for רבי יהושע's reading. רבי שמעון בן יוחאי also learns both ideas from this same פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even though the Romans offered another reading, a great תנא used this פסוק for both תחיית המתים and knowing the future. This shows that the reading 'משה will lie and rise' is a real, accepted way to learn the פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: It was also said (a supporting statement)

phrases.english: It was also said: Rabbi Yoḥanan said
in the name of Rabbi Shimon ben Yoḥai:

phrases.aramaic: מִנַּיִין שֶׁהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא מְחַיֵּה מֵתִים
phrases.english: From where do we know that the Holy One, Blessed be He, brings the dead back to life
and knows what will happen in the future?

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר ״הִנְּךָ שֹׁכֵב עִם אֲבֹתֶיךָ וְקָם וְגוֹ׳״.
phrases.english: As it says: "Behold, you will lie with your fathers and rise, etc."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבי יהושע's reading from step 25 after the challenge in step 26.
steps.raayaObject: Reading 'משה will lie and rise' as a source for תחיית המתים and for knowing the future
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יוחנן in the name of רבי שמעון בן יוחאי

steps.title: רבי אליעזר ברבי יוסי against the books of the כותים
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר ברבי יוסי tells how he proved the כותים wrong when they said the תורה does not teach תחיית המתים.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא teaches: רבי אליעזר ברבי יוסי said: With this I proved the books of the כותים false, since they said there is no תחיית המתים in the תורה. I said to them: You changed your תורה, and it got you nothing, since you still say there is no תחיית המתים in the תורה.
steps.whatsHappening: A new ברייתא begins. רבי אליעזר ברבי יוסי sets up his debate with the כותים, who said the תורה has no source for תחיית המתים. His actual proof comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He tells the כותים that their changes to the תורה did not help them. Even in their own תורה there is still a hint to life after death, as he will show.

keyTerms.meaning: The dead coming back to life

phrases.aramaic: תַּנְיָא: אָמַר רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי:
phrases.english: It is taught: Rabbi Eliezer, son of Rabbi Yosei, said:
With this matter I proved the books of the Samaritans false,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁהָיוּ אוֹמְרִים אֵין תְּחִיַּית הַמֵּתִים מִן הַתּוֹרָה.
phrases.english: for they would say there is no resurrection of the dead from the Torah.
I said to them: You falsified your Torah,
and you gained nothing by it,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאַתֶּם אוֹמְרִים אֵין תְּחִיַּית הַמֵּתִים מִן הַתּוֹרָה.
phrases.english: since you say there is no resurrection of the dead from the Torah.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא: אָמַר רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new source for תחיית המתים, in a debate with the כותים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The כותים are wrong to say the תורה has no source for תחיית המתים.

steps.title: 'His sin is upon him' points to עולם הבא
steps.stepSummary: If 'cut off' is punishment in this world, then 'his sin is upon him' must mean punishment later, in עולם הבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'That soul shall surely be cut off; his sin is upon him.' 'Surely be cut off' means in this world. 'His sin is upon him': when is that? Isn't it in עולם הבא?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר ברבי יוסי gives his proof. The punishment in this world is already covered by 'cut off,' so 'his sin is upon him' must refer to a time after death.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the person has been cut off and died, his sin still stays 'upon him.' That only makes sense if there is a life after death, in עולם הבא, where he answers for it. So the תורה does hint to life after death.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall surely be cut off (the punishment of כרת)

steps.whatToRemember: The words 'his sin is upon him' come after the person is already cut off in this world, so they point to עולם הבא.

phrases.english: See, it says: "That soul shall surely be cut off;
that soul, its sin is upon it."
"Shall surely be cut off": in this world.
"Its sin is upon it": for when? Is it not for the World to Come?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the actual proof promised in step 29.
steps.raayaObject: The תורה hints to עולם הבא, life after death

steps.title: Why not prove both punishments from the doubled word
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא asks אביי why רבי אליעזר ברבי יוסי did not learn both this-world and next-world punishment from the doubled word הכרת תכרת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said to אביי: Let him tell them both ideas from the words 'הכרת תכרת'!
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא questions the proof from step 30. He suggests an easier proof that uses just one phrase.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 30, רבי אליעזר needed two parts of the פסוק: 'cut off' and 'his sin is upon him.' רב פפא points out that the פסוק already doubles the word: 'הכרת תכרת.' One half could mean this world and the other half could mean עולם הבא.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Cut off, it shall be cut off': the doubled verb in the פסוק
A leading אמורא, רב פפא's teacher
'Let him say to them': a suggestion that challenges what was actually said

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said to Abaye:
But let him say to them both [ideas]
phrases.notes: 'Him' is רבי אליעזר ברבי יוסי, and 'them' are the כותים from step 29.

phrases.english: from 'it shall be cut off, cut off'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the choice of proof made in step 30
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אליעזר ברבי יוסי's two-part proof
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A simpler proof exists from the doubled verb, so why use a longer one?

steps.title: The doubled word could be dismissed as normal speech
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that the כותים would reply that the תורה just speaks the way people speak.
steps.simpleTranslation: They would have said to him: The תורה spoke in the language of people.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי explains why the doubled-word proof was not used: the כותים would not accept it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: People often double a word just for emphasis. The כותים could say the doubling teaches nothing extra, so it is not a strong proof. That is why רבי אליעזר used a proof they could not brush aside.

keyTerms.meaning: The תורה speaks the way people normally speak, so extra words need not teach anything
'They would have said': the expected reply of the other side

steps.confusionAlert: This is not saying the תורה has extra words for no reason in general. The point is only that this kind of doubling could be read as normal style, so it cannot win an argument with someone who rejects the derivation.

phrases.english: They would have said to him:
The Torah spoke in the language of people.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב פפא's question
steps.terutzResolutionType: The suggested proof is weak against an opponent
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The doubled word is a clear proof for both punishments
steps.terutzMaskana: The doubling can be dismissed as speech style, so a stronger proof was chosen

steps.title: רבי עקיבא: the doubled word teaches both worlds
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows the same question is an argument between תנאים. רבי עקיבא learns this world and עולם הבא from the two halves of הכרת תכרת.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is like a dispute of תנאים: 'הכרת תכרת': 'הכרת' means in this world, 'תכרת' means in עולם הבא. These are the words of רבי עקיבא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא showing that the question of steps 31-32 is an old argument. It first gives רבי עקיבא's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא reads the doubled word the way רב פפא suggested: each half adds a separate punishment. This matches רב פפא's approach. The other side, matching אביי's answer, comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Like the תנאים': this question was already argued by earlier sages
'The words of רבי עקיבא': identifies whose view this is

phrases.english: It is like [a dispute of] Tannaim:
'It shall be cut off, cut off':
'Cut off' means in this world,
'it shall be cut off' means for the World to Come,
these are the words of Rabbi Akiva.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that רב פפא's suggestion matches רבי עקיבא's view
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Each half of הכרת תכרת teaches a separate punishment: this world and עולם הבא

steps.title: רבי ישמעאל: then we would have three worlds
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל objects that the previous פסוק already says ונכרתה. Together with both halves of הכרת תכרת, that would give three cut-offs.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ישמעאל said to him: Doesn't it already say 'He blasphemes ה', and that soul shall be cut off'? Are there three worlds?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ישמעאל attacks רבי עקיבא's reading. It would give one cut-off too many.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק just before already uses 'ונכרתה.' If that word counts, and each half of הכרת תכרת also counts, we end up with three punishments. But there are only two worlds.

keyTerms.meaning: 'But hasn't it already been said': introduces a challenge from another פסוק
'And it shall be cut off': the cut-off word in the earlier פסוק

phrases.english: Rabbi Yishmael said to him:
But has it not already been said:
'He blasphemes the Lord, and [that soul] shall be cut off',
Are there then three worlds?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי עקיבא's reading
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי עקיבא's reading of הכרת תכרת as two separate punishments
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Counting ונכרתה as well gives three cut-offs, but there are only two worlds.

steps.title: רבי ישמעאל's reading: the doubling is just speech style
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל learns this world from ונכרתה and עולם הבא from הכרת. The doubled form teaches nothing, because the תורה speaks like people.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather: 'ונכרתה' means in this world, 'הכרת' means in עולם הבא, and 'הכרת תכרת': the תורה spoke in the language of people.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ישמעאל gives his own reading, which keeps the count at two worlds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He moves the this-world punishment to the earlier פסוק and reads 'הכרת' as עולם הבא. The doubled ending adds nothing new. This matches אביי's answer in step 32.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Rather': introduces the correct reading in place of the rejected one

steps.whatToRemember: רבי עקיבא learns something from each half of הכרת תכרת. רבי ישמעאל says the doubling is just how people speak. Both agree there is punishment in this world and in עולם הבא.

phrases.english: Rather, 'and it shall be cut off' means in this world,
'cut off' means for the World to Come,
and 'it shall be cut off, cut off':
the Torah spoke in the language of people.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a new reading that avoids the three-worlds problem
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-assigning the words of the פסוקים
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Each half of הכרת תכרת teaches a separate world
steps.terutzMaskana: ונכרתה teaches this world, הכרת teaches עולם הבא, and the doubling is speech style

steps.title: What do both תנאים learn from עונה בה
steps.stepSummary: Both תנאים already found both punishments elsewhere, so the גמרא asks what the words עונה בה teach them.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to both רבי ישמעאל and רבי עקיבא, what do they do with 'עונה בה'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what the phrase 'his sin is upon him' comes to teach, since neither תנא needs it for עולם הבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 30, רבי אליעזר used 'עונה בה' to prove punishment in עולם הבא. But רבי עקיבא and רבי ישמעאל both learn עולם הבא from other words. So the phrase seems extra for them.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Its sin is upon it': the end of the פסוק
'What do they do with it?': what does this phrase teach in their view

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל וּבֵין רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא,
phrases.english: According to both Rabbi Yishmael and Rabbi Akiva,
what do they do with 'its sin is upon it'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows from both readings of the תנאים, which leave עונה בה without a job
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the words עונה בה teach according to the תנאים

steps.title: עונה בה teaches that תשובה saves from כרת
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא learns from עונה בה that the sinner is cut off only while his sin is still on him, meaning he has not done תשובה.
steps.simpleTranslation: For what was taught: One might think he is cut off even if he did תשובה. So the פסוק says 'עונה בה': I said it only when his sin is still upon him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the phrase teaches a different law: someone who does תשובה is not cut off.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without these words, one might think כרת is final no matter what. 'His sin is upon him' limits the punishment to a person whose sin is still there. Once he does תשובה, the sin is no longer on him.

keyTerms.meaning: 'One might think': introduces a mistaken possibility
'The פסוק teaches': introduces the words that correct the mistake

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that even the harsh punishment of כרת can be avoided through תשובה.

phrases.english: For that which was taught [in a baraita]:
One might think [he is cut off] even if he repented?
The verse teaches: 'its sin is upon it.'
I said it only
at a time when his sin is upon him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about עונה בה
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: עונה בה teaches that כרת applies only to someone who has not done תשובה

steps.title: קליאופטרא asks: will the dead rise naked or clothed
steps.stepSummary: Queen קליאופטרא accepts תחיית המתים from a פסוק in תהלים and asks רבי מאיר whether the dead will rise naked or in their clothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: Queen קליאופטרא asked רבי מאיר: I know the dead will live, as it says 'They will blossom out of the city like grass of the earth.' But when they rise, will they rise naked or in their clothes?
steps.whatsHappening: A new story begins. Here the questioner already believes in תחיית המתים and only asks about the details.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now the debates were about whether תחיית המתים is in the תורה at all. Here she proves it herself from a פסוק that compares people to sprouting grass. Her question is about what the risen dead will be like.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The dead (literally, those lying down) will live'

phrases.aramaic: שָׁאֲלָה קְלֵיאוֹפַּטְרָא מַלְכְּתָא אֶת רַבִּי מֵאִיר.
phrases.english: Queen Cleopatra asked Rabbi Meir.
She said: I know that the dead will live,
as it is written: 'And they will blossom out of the city like grass of the earth.'
But when they rise,
do they rise naked
or do they rise in their garments?

steps.triggerLanguage: שָׁאֲלָה קְלֵיאוֹפַּטְרָא מַלְכְּתָא אֶת רַבִּי מֵאִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new story about תחיית המתים
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the dead rise naked or clothed

steps.title: רבי מאיר: a קל וחומר from wheat
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר answers that a wheat kernel is planted bare and comes up wrapped in layers, so the righteous, who are buried clothed, will surely rise clothed.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to her: A קל וחומר from wheat. If wheat, which is buried naked, comes out in many garments, then the righteous, who are buried in their clothes, all the more so.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי מאיר answers the queen's question with a קל וחומר from nature.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A bare grain goes into the ground and sprouts with husks and coverings. If something buried with nothing comes up covered, then people buried in their clothes will certainly rise clothed. Her own comparison of the dead to plants becomes the basis of the answer.

keyTerms.meaning: Logic from a lighter case to a stronger one
'All the more so': the conclusion of a קל וחומר

steps.whatToRemember: The righteous will rise in their clothing. This is proven by a קל וחומר from wheat, which goes in bare and comes up covered.

phrases.english: He said to her: It is an a fortiori from wheat.
If wheat, which is buried naked,
phrases.notes: The kernel is planted bare, without its husk.

phrases.english: comes out in several garments,
the righteous, who are buried in their garments,
all the more so [will they rise clothed].

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers קליאופטרא's question
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The righteous will rise clothed, by a קל וחומר from wheat

steps.title: The emperor asks how dust can come back to life
steps.stepSummary: The Roman emperor challenges רבן גמליאל: the dead become dust, and dust cannot live, so how can there be תחיית המתים?
steps.simpleTranslation: The emperor said to רבן גמליאל: You Jews say the dead will come back to life. But they turn into dust, and can dust come to life?!
steps.whatsHappening: A new story begins: the Roman emperor attacks the belief in תחיית המתים with a logical challenge. The גמרא is setting up the answer, which comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The emperor does not question whether a פסוק teaches תחיית המתים. He argues it is impossible: once a body has turned completely into dust, nothing of the person seems left to bring back. This is a stronger attack than קליאופטרא's question, which already accepted תחיית המתים and only asked about clothing.

keyTerms.meaning: The נשיא, the head of the Jewish people, who is being challenged here

steps.confusionAlert: Don't confuse this with the previous story. קליאופטרא believed in תחיית המתים and only asked a detail. The emperor is denying that it can happen at all.

phrases.english: The emperor said to Rabban Gamliel:
You say that the dead will live.
phrases.notes: 'You' here means the Jews in general, not only רבן גמליאל.

phrases.english: But they become dust,
and does dust come to life?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the story of קליאופטרא and רבי מאיר, the גמרא brings another story of an outsider questioning תחיית המתים, this time denying that it is possible.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The dead decay into dust, and dust is lifeless matter, so it seems impossible for them to live again.
